candidates.description: The manual describes an advance-state delivery as exactly four state changes: the revert root hash, the input bytes in the rx buffer, reason/length in htif_fromhost, and iflags_Y = 0. It gives this three times (low-level host loop, its prose, and the send_cmio_response API text) and nowhere says that a delivery writes imcyclemax. 'imcyclemax' occurs five times in the manual (config grammar, default dump, break reasons, register table, and the one-line description 'holds the inclusive mcycle limit'); none says who sets it or to what. The blockchain chapter only says 'each input owns 2^48 mcycles, counted from the state that receives it' and that 'mcycle overflow' is a fixed point. The implementation's delivery additionally (a) writes imcyclemax = mcycle + 2^48 - 1 (saturating), and (b) zero-fills the rx buffer from the end of the input up to the next power of two (minimum 32 bytes), overwriting stale bytes of an earlier, longer input. Both are part of the hashed state, so the transition the manual documents and the transition every emulator path implements produce different states and different root hashes after any delivery. THREAT_MODEL makes the manual the specification of the state transition function ('The manual's documented semantics define it on every state') and itself relies on the undocumented behavior (section 2 imcyclemax, R5 'That delivery records the revert root hash and sets imcyclemax', R6 'imcyclemax is likewise written only by such a delivery').
candidates.trigger: No adversary action is needed: every advance-state delivery that changes the state. The mismatch is visible to anyone who derives or re-implements the delivery from the manual (a second node implementation, a host that follows the documented low-level loop with write_memory/write_reg, an auditor checking the on-chain SendCmioResponse against the manual): their after-state differs from the emulator's and the referee's in imcyclemax (and possibly in the padding bytes).
candidates.reachability: Reachable at every input boundary of every valid template: on the harness template baremetal-template (mcycle 3526372, imcyclemax 0xffffffffffffffff, yielded manual rx-accepted), send_cmio_response sets imcyclemax to 0x100000035cee3; the manual's four steps leave it at 0xffffffffffffffff.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no. Nothing excluded is needed: it is a contradiction between the manual and the delivery transition on the honest operator's path ('Delivering inputs').

2 Role: input delivery is 'Honest operator' in the AUDIT.md table ('... input delivery ...'); the regenerated machine-solidity-step (Referee verifier) has the same writes, so no path disagrees with another: the disagreement is with the manual only.

3 High/Medium cases: matches Medium, 'An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths, in behavior that no correct guest relies on for isolation or data integrity (R7)', through the closing rule of the Medium class: 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right.' The point is security-relevant: section 2 defines 'imcyclemax. The register that holds the last mcycle the current input can reach. Reaching it stops the input. An advance-state delivery that changes the state sets it to the delivery's mcycle plus the mcycle limit per input, minus one', R5 lists 'reaching imcyclemax' as a fixed point, and R13 makes 'The accesses each logged transition makes, and their order' part of the protocol. If the manual were right (a delivery does not touch imcyclemax and writes only the input bytes), all implemented paths deviate together.

4 Critical: only under a literal reading of the definition 'State transition function ... The manual's documented semantics define it on every state ... The uarch program and the verifier code that a deployment fixes on-chain must implement it' together with R3 ('that after-hash must be the canonical hash that the state transition function defines'): then every delivery verified on-chain yields a hash other than the documented one. I do not prefer this reading because the manual's blockchain chapter does state the per-input 2^48 limit and the overflow fixed point, so the intent is documented and only the mechanism is missing.

5 Low: if triage reads the per-input sentences of the blockchain chapter ('each input owns 2^48 mcycles, counted from the state that receives it'; 'BREAK_REASON_MCYCLE_OVERFLOW ... when mcycle reaches imcyclemax') as documenting the write, the remaining defect is an incomplete description (a documentation gap), Low.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (preferred: undocumented, consistent deviation from the manual's documented delivery on a security-relevant point) / Low (if the blockchain chapter's 2^48-per-input sentences count as documenting it) / Critical only under the literal 'manual defines the transition function' reading
candidates.threat_to_goal: The goal is stated relative to 'the state the state transition function defines', and the threat model says the manual's documented semantics define that function. For the delivery form the manual and the deployed verifier disagree on which registers change, so the specification cannot be used to check that the on-chain SendCmioResponse (or a second honest-operator implementation, A6) implements the right function; an operator implementation written from the manual computes other hashes than the referee from the first input on and loses every dispute. It violates the Medium rule on manual contradictions and R13's requirement that the protocol (accesses of each logged transition) be defined.

(different). After additionally writing imcyclemax by hand the two roots are equal, so imcyclemax is the whole difference when the padding is zeroed by hand. grep of doc/README.md: 'imcyclemax' at 3232, 3580, 4042, 7356, 7384 only; no sentence says a delivery sets it; no sentence documents the zero padding of the rx buffer.
candidates.test_idea: Lua test on a valid template: copy A gets machine:send_cmio_response(ADVANCE_STATE, input, root); copy B gets exactly the state changes the manual's host loop lists (revert root hash at AR_SHADOW_REVERT_ROOT_HASH_START, input bytes at AR_CMIO_RX_BUFFER_START, htif_fromhost, iflags_Y). Assert A:get_root_hash() == B:get_root_hash() (fails today: imcyclemax differs; with a previous longer input in the rx buffer the padding bytes differ too). Alternatively a documentation test that asserts the manual's delivery description names every register that log_send_cmio_response reports as written (the access log of a delivery lists a write to imcyclemax at 0x2f8 that the manual does not mention).

candidates.title: Manual says the processor shadow and shadow TLB are address ranges visible to the main processor and discoverable through the PMA array (with a PMA_SHADOW_STATE_DID); the emulator gives them no PMA entry and every guest access faults
candidates.component: Manual doc/README.md ('### The main processor', '### The board', '#### Address ranges', '#### PMAs') versus machine address ranges / interpreter memory access (src/machine-address-ranges.cpp, src/find-pma.hpp, src/interpret.cpp read_virtual_memory_slow)
candidates.location: doc/README.md 7337-7340 ('The processor makes its entire state available, externally and read-only, by mapping every register to the start of the physical address space (in the processor shadow, a 4KiB range)'), 7434-7455 ('Devices are mapped to the processor's physical address space. The mapping can be seen in the following table' listing 0x0-0xfff 'Processor and board shadow', 0x1000-0x6fff 'Shadow TLB', 0x10000 'PMA Array', uarch shadow and uarch RAM), 7875-7880 ('The address ranges visible to the main processor are mapped at fixed positions ... These are the ranges listed in the board mapping table at the start of this chapter ... and discoverable at runtime via the PMA array'), 7896-7898 ('Each address range visible to the main processor is described by an entry in the array of Physical Memory Attribute records'), 7924-7937 (DID table with PMA_SHADOW_STATE_DID = 2); src/machine-address-ranges.cpp:315-318 (shadow state and uarch shadow registered with .pmas = false)
candidates.description: The manual states that the ranges of the board mapping table are the ranges visible to the main processor and that each of them has a PMA entry; the table starts with the processor shadow (registers, revert root hash) and the shadow TLB, the register section says every register is mapped read-only at the start of the physical address space, and the PMA section defines a driver id for the shadow state. Only for the uarch shadow and uarch RAM does the manual add that they are private and have no PMA entry. In the implementation the shadow state range 0x0-0x7fff (registers, revert root hash, shadow TLB) is registered in the hash tree only: the guest-readable PMA array has no entry for it, and a guest load from 0x0, 0x100 (mcycle), 0x2f8 (imcyclemax), 0xfe0 (revert root hash) or 0x1000 (TLB) raises a load access fault. The implementation matches R8 ('Guest memory accesses cannot address the processor registers, the uarch state and uarch memory, the cached translation state, the revert root hash, imcyclemax'), so the defect is the manual's, but it is a contradiction on exactly the containment boundary R8 defines. A guest written from the manual (for example one that reads imcyclemax at 0x2f8 to bound its own mcycle usage, the only way the manual offers to learn that limit) traps instead.
candidates.trigger: Any guest code that follows the manual and reads a register from the processor shadow, or looks for the shadow in the PMA array.
candidates.reachability: Any machine: the PMA array of bugs/harness/work/configs/linux-rootfs has 9 entries (RAM, DTB, flash drive, tx, rx, HTIF, CLINT, PLIC, PMAs) and none for 0x0.
rating_steps: 2 Role: interpreter and state layout, 'Honest operator' in the AUDIT.md table.

3 High/Medium cases: Medium: 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right.' If the manual were right (shadow readable by the guest, read-only), the emulator's refusal is 'An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths, in behavior that no correct guest relies on for isolation or data integrity (R7)'. The point is security-relevant because it is the R8 boundary: 'Guest memory accesses cannot address the processor registers, the uarch state and uarch memory, the cached translation state, the revert root hash, imcyclemax, or the unreproducible mode.'

4 Critical: not claimed; a literal R7 reading ('The emulator implements ... the devices as the manual documents them ... Address translation and memory permissions ... any deviation lets an input subvert a correct guest') would make it Critical, as triage noted as an alternative for R3-VARSPEC-1, but here the deviation only denies an access.
5 Low: if 'externally' in the register section is read as 'to the host only' and the Address-ranges sentence as loose wording, it is a documentation inaccuracy with no rule violated.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (preferred) / Low (if read as loose wording)
candidates.threat_to_goal: Does not break the goal by itself: the emulator enforces R8. It is a contradiction between the manual (the specification the threat model refers to) and the behavior on the guest containment boundary; the Medium class says such a contradiction is a defect in one of the two. Related to, but not the same as, R3-VARSPEC-1 (bit layout of the PMA entries): this is about which ranges have entries and are visible at all.

candidates.title: Manual says the uarch can access all memory ranges and devices visible to the main processor; the native uarch reads device ranges as zero and traps on stores to device ranges and to the PMA array (manual side of the R1-R10-1 divergence)
candidates.component: Manual doc/README.md ('### The microarchitecture') versus the uarch memory map (machine::read_word / machine::write_word in src/machine.cpp, used by uarch_state_access and the log producers)
candidates.role: Honest operator (uarch, log producers); likely a duplicate of R1-R10-1 as far as the store divergence goes
candidates.location: doc/README.md 7393-7397 ('code running in the uarch has access to the entire state of the Cartesi Machine, including the main processor and the entire board'), 7429-7430 ('In addition to being able to access all memory ranges and devices visible to the main processor, the uarch includes a private 2MiB of RAM'); src/machine.cpp:2030-2075 (write_word: shadow padding, device ranges, read-only and 'protected' ranges throw)
candidates.description: R3 defines a uarch trap by the uarch memory map ('an access that its memory map does not allow'), and the manual is the specification. The manual's only statement of that memory map says the uarch can access every memory range and device visible to the main processor. Natively, a uarch store to a device range (HTIF 0x40008000, CLINT 0x2004000, PLIC 0x40100000), to the PMA array (a memory range visible to the main processor) or to an unmapped hole throws, i.e. is a trap; a uarch load from a device address returns 0 on every path rather than the device register (with htif_tohost = 0x0101000000000041, LD from 0x40008000 gives 0, LD from the shadow address 0x330 gives the value). So the documented memory map and the native one differ; R1-R10-1 already showed that the verifiers follow neither side consistently for stores. The pristine uarch reaches devices only through shadow registers, so the differing accesses need a non-pristine uarch state.
candidates.trigger: A uarch state whose program stores to or loads from a device address or stores to the PMA array: not produced by the pristine uarch program.
candidates.reachability: Unreachable from a valid template: the uarch RAM is not addressable by the guest (no PMA entry; probe guest loads at 0x600000 fault) and every mcycle ends with the reset that restores the pristine uarch, whose compiled code only uses shadow-register addresses and memory ranges for the main processor's state.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no (machine API misuse is not needed to state the contradiction; the experiment used write_memory only to build the unreachable uarch state).
2 Role: uarch and log producers, 'Honest operator'.

3 High/Medium cases: for stores this is the divergence R1-R10-1 rated High ('A verifier that misbehaves only on demonstrably unreachable before-states ... accepting a uarch trap, R3' / 'A divergence between paths only at demonstrably unreachable states'); the manual sentence decides which side is wrong (if the manual were right, the native refusal is the defect). For loads, all paths agree and differ from the manual only at unreachable states: Medium at most ('A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point ...'), more plausibly Low.
5 Low: for the load part and if the store part is deduplicated into R1-R10-1.
candidates.claimed_severity: Low on its own (manual wording about the uarch memory map); High only as part of R1-R10-1, which it would duplicate
candidates.threat_to_goal: None at reachable states. It matters for fixing R1-R10-1: the manual's memory-map sentence says the stores the native uarch refuses are allowed, so the fix has to change the manual as well as one of the implementations.
candidates.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r7/MANARCH/udev.lua and umap.lua (uarch RAM patched with 'ld x5,0(x6)' / 'sd x5,0(x6)' through write_memory, one run_uarch step and one log_step_uarch): LD 0x40008000 -> 0 while LD 0x330 -> 0x101000000000041; SD to 0x40008000, 0x2004000, 0x40100000, 0x10000, 0x1000, 0xfe0, 0x8000 -> 'attempted memory write ...' / 'unhandled write to shadow state' (trap) in run_uarch and log_step_uarch; SD to RAM, DTB, rx and tx buffers, uarch RAM, mcycle, imcyclemax, iunrep succeeds. /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r7/MANARCH/uload.lua: loads from device ranges, holes and addresses up to 0xfffffffffffffff8 return 0 natively and their logs verify.
candidates.test_idea: Covered by the R1-R10-1 test for stores. For the manual: a test that builds a uarch state doing 'sd' to AR_HTIF_START and asserts that run_uarch, log_step_uarch + verify_step_uarch and the EVM step all agree with what the manual's uarch memory map says (allowed), or that the manual lists the ranges the uarch may store to.

not_covered: Sentence-by-sentence check done for doc/README.md 7270-8128; found consistent with the code or by experiment (no candidate): register table and offsets (856 bytes, 107 registers, 43 control, last 8 device registers), semantics of iprv/iflags_X/iflags_Y/iflags_H/icycleinstret/iunrep/imcyclemax as read from interpret(), uarch shadow table and 52-instruction RV64I decoder, board memory map constants, default pc and a1, mtimecmp reset value, divisor 8192, CLINT MTIP update on mtimecmp write and at ticks, HTIF offsets/fields/devices/commands/reasons, 'unavailable commands are silently ignored', halt honored with ihalt = 0, getchar/putchar formats, PMA DID values and sentinel, the printed DTB (the manual's dtc command run on the rootfs-docs image reproduces the listing byte for byte, 118 lines), EvmAdvance/Voucher/Notice signatures. Known contradictions (Sv48, PMA istart layout, CLINT msip, flash placement) were not re-reported.

Page tables outside RAM ('raises the access fault of the original access type'): checked by reading translate_virtual_address/read_ram_uint64 only. My dynamic test (MPRV with MPP=S, root table in the tx buffer) was badly designed and its result is not usable; PTEs inside a flash drive or NVRAM and the fetch case were not run.

Native-versus-uarch differential was run only for one bare-metal guest (AMO/LR-SC/FSD on HTIF tohost, CLINT msip and mtimecmp, PLIC claim, automatic and manual yields, S-level interrupt bits set from M-mode, mideleg toggles; 77,940 mcycles, root hashes equal after every mcycle, at most 2,973 uarch cycles per mcycle). No S/U-mode, no Linux workload, no Solidity/EVM replay of these steps.

The '#### Rollup' guest loop was checked against the emulator side only (send_cmio_response, HTIF yield); libcmt, the rollup tool and rollup-http-server were not compared with the pseudo-code (e.g. the root written after an inspect, the reject of an unknown request type).
The manual's host loop for inspect-state requests and for exceptions was read against send_cmio_response only; cartesi-machine's own rollup loop was not compared with it.

PLIC: the manual documents only its address range and DTB node; register semantics (single context at 0x2000/0x200004 while the DTB advertises two) need a VirtIO source, so an unreproducible machine; not pursued.
VirtIO devices (unreproducible only): whether more than 16 devices leave the documented 0x40010000-0x4001ffff window was not checked.

Flash drive and NVRAM placement rules of the board section (start after RAM, 64 TiB, 2 MiB alignment, 128 TiB NVRAM length): not re-tested (R3-VARSPEC-5 was dropped by triage). I only confirmed that the config chapter's rules (start aligned to the length rounded up to a power of two, no overlap of rounded-up ranges) and the reserved uarch gaps are enforced, and that an NVRAM is accepted in the free gaps 0x8000-0xffff, 0x11000-0x3fffff and in the VirtIO window of a reproducible machine.

Linux/OpenSBI side of '### Linux setup' (OpenSBI within the 512 KiB no-map region, kernel payload at 0x80200000, PLIC fixup to 0xffffffff, removal of rng-seed from /sys/firmware/fdt) is out of scope and was only observed, not audited. The fixed 4096-byte rng-seed the emulator puts in /chosen is not mentioned by the manual (guest randomness is predictable by design); not reported.
Worst-case uarch cycles per mcycle and the uarch asserts (NDEBUG is not defined for the uarch build; 13 abort call sites in the pristine image) were not re-examined; earlier rounds covered them.

Text typos of the slice were ignored on purpose (e.g. 'memory@80000000 describes 64MiB' next to reg = 0x8000000, the HTIF table's reserved offsets ending at 0x218, the shadow state range being 0x0-0x7fff while the table lists 0x0-0x6fff).
Manual chapters outside 7270-8128 were read only where they restate facts of this slice (send_cmio_response API text, config defaults, break reasons, per-input 2^48 limit).
